bandhas.name: Mūla Bandha
bandhas.action: Gently contract and lift the pelvic floor at the perineum, drawing it up and in.
bandhas.locks: Stops apāna (the downward breath) from escaping below and turns it upward, toward the navel.
bandhas.phases: Held in both internal and external retention.
benefits: Steadies the base of the spine and the seat
Turns apāna upward to meet prāṇa at the navel
Haṭha texts describe it as rousing energy at Mūlādhāra
bandhas.caution: Use a light contraction, not a strain. Avoid during menstruation, pregnancy or with pelvic-floor conditions without guidance.

bandhas.name: Uḍḍīyāna Bandha
bandhas.action: After a full exhalation, draw the abdomen in toward the spine and up under the ribs.
bandhas.locks: Lifts the diaphragm and draws the united prāṇa-apāna from the navel up into Suṣumṇā.
bandhas.phases: Only in external retention (breath held out), never with the lungs full.
benefits: Massages the abdominal organs; traditionally said to kindle the digestive fire (agni)
Lifts energy from the navel toward the heart
Called in Haṭha texts the lion that conquers the elephant of death
bandhas.caution: Only on an empty stomach and with the breath held out. Avoid with high blood pressure, heart conditions, hernia, ulcers, pregnancy or recent abdominal surgery.

bandhas.name: Jālandhara Bandha
bandhas.action: Lengthen the back of the neck and lower the chin toward the top of the breastbone; lift the chest slightly to meet it.
bandhas.locks: Seals the throat so prāṇa does not rise and escape upward during retention, and protects the head from pressure.
bandhas.phases: Held in both internal and external retention; release it before breathing again.
benefits: Keeps retention comfortable by sealing the airway
Traditionally said to calm the heart and the mind
Contains prāṇa below the throat during the hold
bandhas.caution: Do not strain the neck. Lift the head fully before inhaling or exhaling. Avoid with cervical spine problems.

pranayamas.name: Kumbhaka Prāṇāyāma
pranayamas.about: Inhale for one count, hold the breath in (antara kumbhaka) for four, exhale for two and hold the breath out (bāhya kumbhaka) for two, then repeat. During the holds the bandhas seal prāṇa inside: Mūla and Jālandhara during the internal hold, all three (Mahā Bandha) during the external hold.
benefits: Lengthens and steadies the breath; trains calm during retention
With the bandhas, joins prāṇa and apāna at the navel and directs them into Suṣumṇā
Traditionally prepares the mind for concentration (dhāraṇā)
pranayamas.caution: Build up slowly: start with a short count and few rounds, never strain or gasp. Stop if dizzy. Avoid long holds with high blood pressure, heart or lung conditions or in pregnancy; learn retention with a qualified teacher.

pranayamas.name: Sama Vṛtti
pranayamas.about: Equal counts for inhalation, internal hold, exhalation and external hold — a gentle introduction to retention. Bandhas may be added in the holds as in Kumbhaka Prāṇāyāma.
benefits: A calm, easy rhythm for beginners
pranayamas.caution: Keep every count comfortable; shorten the holds if the breath becomes strained.
